fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Lead Score
fields.features_subheading: Each part adds, removes, or explains points, and every change lands in the lead's score history.
fields.feature_1:
Every point saved with the rule that gave it

Each point a lead earns is stored with the rule behind it and the date. A rep who opens the record sees 25 for the title and 15 for the pricing page, not one number to take on faith.
fields.feature_2:
Fit and activity kept as two scores

Who the lead is and what the lead does are scored apart. A strong fit with no activity reads differently from a busy visitor at the wrong company, and you set a threshold for each.
fields.feature_3:
Points off for quiet leads and bad signals

Set rules that subtract points: 10 for every 30 quiet days, more for a student email or a careers page visit. Old interest fades, and the score reflects what the lead is doing now.
fields.feature_4:
Scores written back to your CRM record

Connect HubSpot or any CRM with an API, and the app writes the current score and its parts to each contact. Reps work from the score in the screen they already use every day.
fields.feature_5:
A message when a lead crosses the line

When a lead passes your threshold, its owner gets a Slack message or an email naming the lead and the points that moved it. A lead that falls back below the line leaves the queue.
fields.feature_6:
Your scoring app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of the scoring app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can read every point rule in the source and change it the way any other code is changed.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Ways a Lead Score Moves
fields.tab_content_1:
A VP title and 400 employees earn 50 fit points

Pinecastle Routing scores every demo form on fit. Halvard Steinsland, VP of Operations at Quellbrook Haulage, gets 25 points for his title. The size rule pays 25 at 200 or more employees, and his company has 400. Any lead with 40 or more fit points reaches Odalys Ferreira, an account executive, by direct message.
fields.tab_content_2:
12 bookings by day 4 make the trial product qualified

Kitebrook scores each trial on what its team does in the app. Marrowfield Dental invites 3 teammates for 25 points and connects a calendar for 20. Its 12 bookings clear the 10-booking rule for 30 more: 75 points on day 4. At 70 the account is product qualified, and its owner, Benedikt Aaltonen, gets a direct message.
fields.tab_content_3:
After 60 quiet days, 72 points become 52

Rosalind Achterhof of Coldharbour Clinics reached 72 points with Tidewell Payroll, above its 60-point sales line. Then she went quiet. The app takes 10 points off for every 30 days with no activity: 62 after the first 30 days, 52 after 60. Below 60, she leaves Idris Pemberton's call list and goes back to the nurture emails.
fields.tab_content_4:
Marketing ops hears when 9 rejections share a reason

Larkfield Analytics reps rejected 14 of the 90 leads sent to sales last month, each with a reason. Nine said student or job seeker, 3 were outside the sales region, and 2 were duplicates. Any reason given 5 or more times in a month reaches Esperanza Vollmer in marketing ops by direct message.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Lead Scoring Automation
fields.howto_description: Seven steps from your won deals to lead scoring automation with point rules and a sales line, built with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pull the deals you won and lost
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the points and one sales line
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add the rules that take points away
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull the last 50 deals you won and 50 you lost. For each, note what the buyer looked like before the first call and what they did first: job title, company size, industry, the pages they read, the trial actions they took. Those patterns become your first rules.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Keep two numbers per lead, fit and activity, and cap each at 50 so neither can carry a lead to sales alone. Fit comes from form fields and company data. Activity comes from page views and trial actions. List no more than 8 signals for each.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each signal points in line with how often it appeared in won deals compared with lost ones. Then pick one threshold where a lead goes to sales. Start it where roughly a third of last quarter's leads would have crossed, and adjust from there.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write the rules that subtract points: a personal email address, a careers page visit, an unsubscribe. Decide how fast activity points fade when a lead goes quiet. Keep fit points fixed unless the company's data changes, since a quiet VP is still a VP.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Connect the CRM and product data
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect your CRM, your forms, and your product's event data through their APIs. Describe the point rules and the threshold in a prompt, and Emergent builds the scoring app, a score history on each lead, and the alerts that reach each lead's owner.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test the rules on last quarter's leads
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last quarter's leads through the rules before anything goes live, and compare each score with what happened. Closed deals should sit near the top. If a lost lead outscores a won one, find the signal that lifted it and change its points by prompting.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live for one segment first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn scoring on for one segment, such as inbound demo requests, and leave the rest on the old process for a month. Then sit down with sales to read the scores that missed, and change one rule at a time so you can see what each change did.

faq_plan.a: Lead scoring automation is software that gives each lead points by rules you set and updates the score as new data arrives. Points come from who the lead is, such as title and company size, and from what the lead does, such as a pricing page visit. When the score crosses a threshold, the lead goes to sales.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up lead scoring automation?
faq_plan.a: Start from your won and lost deals, list the signals that separate them, and give each one a point value. Add negative points, then choose the score that sends a lead to a rep. In Emergent's AI automation builder, you describe those rules in plain English and get a working scoring app with its database.

faq_plan.q: Which signals should lead scoring automation count?
faq_plan.a: Count the signals that showed up more often in won deals than in lost ones, and nothing else. For fit, that means title, company size, industry, and region. For activity, it means high-intent actions such as a demo request or a teammate invite in a trial. Leave out anything every lead does, such as opening the welcome email.

faq_plan.q: Should lead scoring automation write scores into the CRM?
faq_plan.a: Yes, write the current score to the CRM record where reps work, and keep the rules and the full score history in the scoring app. Emergent builds that app so the history sits in a database you own. Assignment and follow-up tasks belong to your crm automation, which can read the same score field.

faq_plan.q: Should lead scoring automation require a minimum fit score?
faq_plan.a: Yes, set a minimum fit score as well as a total. A total score alone lets a student who reads every blog post reach sales. A minimum fit score, such as 20 of 50, keeps activity from carrying a lead that sales cannot sell to. A minimum activity score does the reverse and keeps a perfect-fit lead who never engaged out of the call list.

faq_plan.q: Should lead scoring automation ever lower a score?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Take points off when a lead shows a reason not to buy, such as a personal email address, and lower activity points after each quiet month. Without both, a lead who was busy in March still looks ready in September. The score history shows a rep which rule took the points and when.

faq_plan.q: What should lead scoring automation do with leads too cold for sales?
faq_plan.a: Send them back to nurture: keep them warm with emails matched to what they showed interest in, and let the score keep counting. A lead that crosses the line later goes to sales then. Run this as a marketing automation workflow that reads the score, so a lead leaves the emails the day it qualifies.

faq_plan.q: How do I measure the results of lead scoring automation?
faq_plan.a: Group leads into score bands, such as under 40, 40 to 59, and 60 and up, and compare how often each band turns into a deal. A working model shows a clear step up between bands. If the middle band converts as well as the top, a signal is overweighted. The app Emergent builds can show those bands on a live dashboard.

faq_plan.q: Should lead scoring automation use AI or point rules?
faq_plan.a: Start with point rules, and add AI once you have the history for it. A model trained on past won and lost deals weighs the signals for you, but its reasons are harder for a rep to check than a point rule. Give a model a few hundred closed deals to learn from before you trust its scores over them.

faq_plan.q: How should a small sales team start with lead scoring automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with fit alone. A team of 2 or 3 reps cannot call every lead, and a few fit rules on the demo form, such as role and headcount, decide which leads get a call today. Add activity points once the team has a month of outcomes, and feed the score into the rest of your sales automation.

plan.angle: No top 10 in the workbook; the ranking pages for lead scoring are CRM vendor docs and explainers that describe point models in general terms. This page shows the app that runs four concrete scoring jobs: fit points from the demo form, product-usage points in a trial, points that fade when a lead goes quiet, and rep rejection reasons counted so marketing ops can fix a rule. It stays on the score itself and leaves routing, nurture emails and CRM hygiene to the crm automation, lead nurturing and sales automation pages. The FAQ answers which signals to count, where the score lives, the threshold, negative points, testing and AI scoring, as operator advice.
